notes.decision: Two ornament/jewel-class nouns of uncertain identity. ⲧⲁⲕⲗⲉⲕ: tentatively 'pearl-ornament' (cf. ⲕⲗⲉⲕⲗⲱⲕ 'round, pearl-like'). ⲥⲗⲁⲡⲗⲉⲡ: reduplicated form, tentatively 'cluster-pieces' or 'fragments.' Together with ⲣ̄ϩⲱϥ-robes and the elements of the cross, they form the chapter's catalog of garment-and-jewel terms whose mystical meanings are to be explained.

Untranslated/transliterated as 'Rhōph-work.' Etymology unclear — possibly related to ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'burn' (as embroidered/scorched-pattern fabric), to ⲗⲏⲃϣ/ⲣⲏⲃϣ 'covering,' or a specialized Lyc. textile term. Flagged for parallels.

ⲟⲃ̄ = Coptic numeral 72; this is the chapter number for the new kephalaion that begins here. The numeral appears repeated (lines 9, 11) likely as decorative marginalia framing the chapter title block. Preserved in the transcription line-by-line.

Read as Lyc. ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉϥ 'he said to him' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ 'he said'), with scribal ⲝ for ⲭ. Functions as standard Kephalaia narrative speech-introducer. Not the Greek-derived ⲧⲁⲝⲟ 'appoint' (which would not take a direct-speech complement).

Read with diaeresis as nomen sacrum ⲓⲏⲥ̄ 'Jesus' preceded by ⲛ̄ⲧⲁ- 'of/that of.' Both occurrences in line 18 = 'of Jesus,' i.e. the disciples are recalling sayings/garments associated with Jesus that they had read in scripture.

Series of qualitative-circumstantial verbs describing the soul's condition in matter: 'afflicted, being slain, being strangled, dead.' ϩⲗ̄ϩⲁⲗⲧ̄ reduplicated 'agitated/afflicted'; ϩⲁⲧⲃⲉ 'kill, slay'; ϩⲱ̄ϩⲁⲱⲧ reduplicated 'strangled, oppressed'; ⲙⲁⲩⲧ qualitative 'dead.' The fourfold death-language describes the captive Living Soul in the body of the Enemy.

Translated 'they are sealed' on the basis of root ⲧⲱⲃⲉ/ⲧⲁⲃⲉϩ 'seal, imprint' (in glossary). The names are 'written and sealed' in scripture — a doublet of inscriptional permanence. Alternative reading 'they are spoken/proclaimed' (from ⲧⲁⲩⲟ) is possible but less likely given the immediately preceding ⲥⲉⲥⲏϩ 'they are written.'

Translated 'the five noeric ones.' Greek νοερόν 'pertaining-to-mind, intellectual.' Manichaean technical term for the five intellectual emanations / faculties (cf. ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ, ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ, ⲧⲥⲃⲱ, ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ, ⲡⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ in glossary). 'Noeric' preserves the Greek technical register; 'intellectual' would also work but flattens the philosophical specificity.

Read as feminine relative ⲧⲉⲧ- + qualitative ⲁⲙⲉⲕ from ⲱⲙⲕ 'swallow, devour' (cf. ⲱⲙⲕ in line 17 same root). Translated 'that has been swallowed' — referring to the Power-of-Light absorbed/concealed in the cosmic body, a standard Manichaean motif. Confidence moderate; alternative reading 'that is fastened' (from ⲧⲱⲙⲉ) cannot be excluded.

Translated 'the Splendid One.' From ⲥⲃⲟⲩⲃⲟⲩ 'be smooth, polished, bright' (Crum 320a). The substantive with article functions as a divine title for the cosmic figure that 'blazes, manifested in the stars.' Capitalized as cosmic principle.

Parsed as ⲉⲧ- (relative) + ⲍⲁ-ⲣⲁ-ϩ = Lyc. ϩⲁ-ⲣⲁⲧ⸗ϥ 'at-his-foot, under him.' Translated 'that is under him, the Omophoros' — fits the cosmography of three earths beneath the Omophoros's head. Lycopolitan ⲍ for ϩ and -ϩ for 3sg.m suffix -ϥ.

Both terms left transliterated. ⲗⲁⲕⲗⲉⲕ likely a reduplicated qualitative meaning 'soft, smooth' (cf. ⲗⲁⲕⲗⲱⲕ); ⲗⲁⲡⲗⲡ possibly 'gleam, twinkle' (cf. ⲗⲗⲡ̄ 'shine'). The two terms function as adjectival modifiers of the great garments, characterizing them by softness/brilliance respectively. Without parallel attestations, retained as Coptic.

Translated 'the pluckers' from ϣⲗ̄ 'pluck (fruits, hair).' Plural relative form 'those who pluck' fits the harvest-typology of the cosmic Power consuming Hyle in the five worlds. Alternative 'branches/clusters' from ϣⲗⲉ 'twig' is also possible.

Translated 'tunics of work.' Greek χιτών 'tunic' + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲣⲍⲱⲃ (Lyc. ⲣ̄-ⲍⲱⲃ 'doing-of-work,' from ϩⲱⲃ 'work'). The 'work-tunics' = the three garments (wind, fire, water) the Living Spirit wears for cosmogonic operations.

Translated 'poured forth the places of ferrying.' ⲙⲁⲛϫⲓⲟⲣⲉ = ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄-ϫⲓ-ⲟⲟⲣⲉ 'place of ferrying-across' (from ϫⲓⲟⲟⲣ 'cross over, ferry'). Refers to cosmic conveyance-points by which the Living Spirit transports light upward — paralleling the cosmic chariots/ships motif.

Translated 'the Cross of Light.' Standard Manichaean technical term (σταυρὸς τοῦ φωτός) for the cosmic Cross — the Living Soul/Jesus patibilis stretched across all matter. The structural parallel of this passage with the prior categories (great garments, splendid one, icons, elements) confirms the editor's restoration.

Translated 'the Dry one and the Moist one,' substantival qualitatives. ⲡⲡⲉⲧⲁⲅⲃⲉ corresponds to ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲇⲃⲉ in the accumulated vocabulary ('the moist one'); the ⲅ-spelling is a Lyc. orthographic variant. The chapter title precedes the leer, then the body begins with the identification of these elemental principles with the Manichaean Calling-and-Hearing dyad.

Translated 'the Counsel of the Living-One.' ⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ = ϣⲟϫⲛⲉ 'counsel' (per glossary ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ); ⲡⲧⲱⲛⲍ̄ = ⲡⲧⲱⲛϩ̄ 'the Living One' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ; cf. ⲡⲧⲱⲛϩ̄ in glossary). The construction identifies this title as the dyad Calling-and-Hearing — a clear correspondential identification.

Translated 'the powers' (tentative). The form ⲅⲁⲙ is unattested in the glossary; in context 'fills in all the X' the most likely sense is 'powers' (= Lyc. ⲛⲓⲟⲁⲙ 'powers' or possibly ⲇⲩⲛⲁⲙⲓⲥ in compressed form). Recurs in line 7 as †ⲅⲁⲙ 'the power.' Confidence moderate.

Translated 'that which fills' (qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill,' Lyc. ⲙⲁⲍⲉ). Confirmed by parallel ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲙⲁⲍⲉ 'in order that they may be filled' in line 5 — same root with causative purpose construction. Alternative reading ⲙⲁⲉⲉ 'walk' (in glossary) is possible but the purposive 'that they may be filled' fits the soul-in-fruit imagery better.

Tentatively parsed as ⲉⲧⲁⲩ-ⲛⲧⲉ-ⲑⲩⲁⲩ 'which they have brought to them' — relative perfect of ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'bring' with dative 3pl suffix. The -ⲑⲩ- spelling for dative-marker is unusual; could be Lyc. variant. Confidence low.

Translated tentatively 'embraces.' ⲭⲱⲡⲙⲉ is uncertain — possibly related to ϩⲱⲡ 'fasten' or ϩⲱⲱⲡ 'embrace'; could alternatively relate to ⲕⲱⲡ 'lair, hidden place' or to a contact-verb. The ⲉϩ- prefix is the Lyc. circumstantial 3sg.m (= Sah. ⲉϥ-). Sequence with 'awakens... gives breadth... embraces(?)' fits the soteriological action of the Soul.

Translated as a fourfold qualitative chain describing the Soul: 'afflicted, slain, troubled, dead.' ⲍⲗⲍⲁⲗⲧ reduplicated form likely from ϩⲗⲟⲗ/ϩⲱⲗϫ 'lament, be afflicted'; ⲍⲁⲧⲃⲉ qualitative of ϩⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'kill'; ⲍⲉϣⲍⲁϣⲧ reduplicated of ϩⲟϣ 'afflict, oppress'; ⲙⲁⲩⲧ qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩ 'die.' Standard Manichaean characterization of the Living Soul in the bonds of matter.

Translated 'the power of the fruits of every kind.' †ⲅⲁⲙ taken as substantival 'the power' (parallel to ⲛⲓⲅⲁⲙ in line 3); †ⲅⲉ tentatively 'every kind/sort' — possibly Lyc. for ⲧϯⲉ or related. Both lexemes uncertain, flagged for parallel research.

Translated 'pound them' — reduplicated form of ⲡⲧⲱⲧ 'fall, knock down,' giving iterative 'pound, crush repeatedly.' Fits the agricultural sequence 'crush — break — pound — give as nourishment' to the worlds of flesh.

Tentatively 'which she crushes by tearing it forth.' ⲣⲡⲧⲗⲅⲉ probably ⲣ̄- + Greek πληγή 'blow,' so 'strike, beat'; ⲗⲗⲁⲩⲗⲉϩ reduplicated form, possibly from ⲣⲁⲩⲣⲉϩ 'tear apart' or ⲗⲱⲗⲉϩ 'writhe.' Both flagged for further research.
Translated 'unto this end.' ⲁⲏ = Lyc. ϩⲁⲏ 'end, last' (cf. ⲡⲓⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ ⲛ̄ⲍⲁⲉ 'this last bōlos' in glossary). The phrase concludes the description of the Soul's torment.

Translated 'her other entire kind also.' †ⲕⲉⲧⲁⲓⲉ = ⲧⲕⲉⲧⲁⲓⲉ 'the other kind' (ⲧⲁⲓⲉ in glossary as 'kind, category'); ⲁⲛ ⲧⲏⲣⲥ = 'also entire'; ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲥ = possessive 'hers.' Refers to another mode of the Soul's affliction.

Parsed as ⲉⲥ-ⲧⲣ̄(ⲉϥ?)-ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'while she causes (it) to shine forth' — circumstantial of causative giving-light. Fits the cosmological imagery of the unified Soul shining forth from one source before division.

Translated 'the first contest.' ⲡⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ = ⲡϣⲟⲣⲡ̄ 'the first' (with ⲧ- as scribal prefixed article). ⲡⲁⲅⲱⲛ = the primordial cosmic battle (per glossary). The kephalaion identifies the multiplication of the Soul's likenesses with the first cosmic struggle.

Translated 'the Enemy' — substantival ϫⲁϫⲉ 'enemy' with definite article, capitalized as cosmic principle (= Hyle/Darkness). The Soul's first substance was sent forth from its proper region 'against the Enemy,' marking the cosmogonic mission.
